plan.summary: This 4-week block gives you one efficient full-body strength and power session each week that fits around higher boxing and sparring volume. Week 1 establishes baseline strength with a simple multi-rep assessment on the main lift so later loading can be set more accurately, and the main build starts in Week 2. Because you are off-camp with only one S&C day and more sport work, the goal is to raise your general force and explosiveness without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build foundational lower-body strength and simple explosive ability with low-complexity work that does not interfere with boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress strength and power with slightly heavier loading while keeping total volume tight enough for sparring recovery.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift toward faster, sharper power and speed expression while holding onto the strength built earlier.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height you can land on quietly and confidently. Step down between reps and keep each jump fast and crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no safe box setup is available. Reset between reps and jump for height.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want the simplest low-impact option. Start from a controlled quarter squat and explode up.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with small jumps in load until you reach one hard, clean top set. Stop before form breaks and keep the depth consistent.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. This establishes your baseline for future percentage work.

performanceTarget.prompt: Record the load and reps from your best top set.

substitutionOptions.name: Goblet Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if barbell back squat setup feels too technical. Push the knees out and stay tall through the torso.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if available and it feels more stable on your shoulders and upper back.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: Use a controlled lower and a strong press without bouncing. Leave 1-2 clean reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Barbell Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you prefer a barbell setup and can keep good control.

substitutionOptions.name: Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler bodyweight option. Keep the body straight and stop before form breaks.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Pull the elbows back with a brief squeeze at the top. Keep the chest planted on the pad and avoid jerking.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the chest-supported station is busy. Keep the torso stable and pull toward the hip.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simple machine-based row with steady tension.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.notes: Move slowly out, keep ribs down, and stop before the lower back arches.

substitutionOptions.name: Stability Ball Rollout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the ab wheel is too demanding right now.

substitutionOptions.name: Cable Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor space or shoulder comfort makes rollouts awkward.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Keep ground contact short before takeoff and land softly. Stop the set if jump height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no box is available. Reset fully between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Trap Bar Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if you can perform it confidently and keep every rep fast and light.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Brace hard, stay balanced through the foot, and drive up fast. Use the training max from Week 1 and keep all sets technically clean.

performanceTarget.prompt: Log all work sets so the app can track your estimated strength trend.

substitutionOptions.name: Safety Bar Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it lets you squat more comfortably and consistently.

substitutionOptions.name: Goblet Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if barbell squats still feel too unstable. Increase load only if depth and posture stay solid.
